question: Should OpenClaw accept the legacy Installed Apps opt-in reset and ship this Google Play disclosure/Data Safety rollout once the branch is refreshed?
rationale: The patch is privacy-protective and focused, but disabling existing opt-ins and adding a Google Play Data Safety release lane are upgrade and release-policy choices automation should not decide.

options.title: Accept reset and rollout
options.body: Approve the legacy opt-in reset, verify Play Console/Data Safety/privacy materials, refresh the branch, and land the PR.

options.title: Revise disclosure first
options.body: Request wording, placement, consent-version, or release-lane changes if Play review or product policy needs a different prominent-disclosure shape.

options.title: Hold for release materials
options.body: Keep the PR open but unmerged until the Data Safety CSV, Play Console state, privacy policy, and review artifacts are ready to ship together.

recommendation.title: Accept reset and rollout
recommendation.body: Approve the legacy opt-in reset, verify Play Console/Data Safety/privacy materials, refresh the branch, and land the PR.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main Android settings and Fastlane history makes this the best available routing owner for the conflict refresh and rollout decision.
